bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to game and fish; prohibiting sale, manufacture, and use of lead tackle; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapters 97C; 325E.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[97C.326] LEAD TACKLE.

Subdivision 1.

Definitions.

For purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given:

(1) "jig" means a weighted hook. Jig does not include lead fishing-related items, including but not limited to fishing line, flies, lures, or spoons; and

(2) "sinker" means a device that is designed to be attached to a fishing line and intended to sink the line. Sinker does not include artificial lures, weighted line, weighted flies, or jig heads.

Subd. 2.

Prohibition.

A person may not use a sinker or jig to take fish if the sinker or jig contains lead and:

(1) weighs one ounce or less; or

(2) measures 2-1/2 inches or less in length.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

This section is effective July 1, 2027.

Sec. 2.

[325E.3895] LEAD TACKLE.

Subdivision 1.

Definitions.

For purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given:

(1) "jig" means a weighted hook. Jig does not include lead fishing-related items, including but not limited to fishing line, flies, lures, or spoons; and

(2) "sinker" means a device that is designed to be attached to a fishing line and intended to sink the line. Sinker does not include artificial lures, weighted line, weighted flies, or jig heads.

Subd. 2.

Manufacture prohibited.

A person may not manufacture for sale in Minnesota a sinker or jig that contains lead and:

(1) weighs one ounce or less; or

(2) measures 2-1/2 inches or less in length.

Subd. 3.

Sale prohibited.

A person may not offer for sale or sell any sinker or jig if it contains lead and:

(1) weighs one ounce or less; or

(2) measures 2-1/2 inches or less in length.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

This section is effective July 1, 2027.
